problem: Classical image-based visual servoing has strong couplings between image features and motion, works only over limited view ranges, and visual navigation of mobile robots lacked a complete set of reactive visual behaviors relying solely on vision.
motivation: Service robots doing pickup and delivery need robust vision-based navigation, object recognition and manipulation without models or prior environment structuring. Using the same visual representation for recognition and pose alignment, and extending servoing over large view ranges, would make vision a universal sensor for mobile manipulation.
key_idea: Decouple gaze and navigation control through a virtual camera plane, use augmented image features with minimal moment-motion couplings, and switch between intermediate reference views (planning in view space) to enable large-view, time-optimal visual servoing.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The thesis claims that decoupled control (virtual camera plane, augmented image moments with only four off-diagonal couplings) and reference-view switching let the same natural landmarks/features be used across a large workspace.
method: Virtual camera plane: decouples gaze control from navigation control so a visual controller can use the same natural landmarks over a large range of motion for mobile robots
Reactive visual behaviors: a door-passing behavior and an omnivision-based obstacle avoidance behavior complete the repertoire for vision-only navigation
Augmented image features: visual servoing with only four off-diagonal couplings between visual moments and degrees of motion
Shared object representation: recognition and manipulator pose alignment use the same unique image features
Multi-reference-view servoing: intermediate reference views with path planning in view space, switching views to minimize time to convergence (model-free)

setting.backbone: classical image-based visual servoing controllers (no learned model)
setting.observation: monocular camera and omnidirectional vision (image features/moments)
setting.action_space: continuous velocity control of mobile platform and manipulator end-effector
setting.simulator: virtual reality simulation plus real platform

results: The abstract reports that the proposed visual control schemes were evaluated successfully in virtual reality and on a real mobile platform and two different manipulators, in realistic unstructured office environments. No quantitative results are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, with no quantitative results
Classical servoing needs reference views and recognizable features, which are perceivable only in limited regions of the workspace
